title: Garlic, Potato and Almond Skordalia with Crisp Fried Cod
summary: Floury potatoes are riced and beaten with a blended paste of almonds, raw garlic and lemon, then loosened with olive oil into a silky dip. Fingers of cod in a light sparkling-water batter are fried until crisp and served alongside with lemon.
equipment: large heavy pot or deep fryer (at least 4 l)
wire rack set over a tray

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as russet or Maris Piper), peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
garlic cloves, peeled and halved, any green shoots removed
extra-virgin olive oil, plus a little to drizzle
fine sea salt or table salt
skinless cod or haddock fillet, cut into 5 x 2 cm fingers
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the potatoes
steps.text: Rinse the potato cubes, simmer until very tender, then let them steam dry.

steps.title: Make the almond paste
steps.text: Blend the almonds, garlic, lemon juice and cold water until smooth.

steps.title: Finish the skordalia
steps.text: Rice the potatoes, stir in the almond paste and beat in the olive oil and salt by hand.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat the frying oil to 180 °C and dust the cod in flour.

steps.title: Batter and fry
steps.text: Whisk the cold batter, dip the cod and fry in batches until crisp and 63 °C inside.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the hot fish with the skordalia and lemon wedges.

tips: Never blend the potatoes; they turn gluey. Rice or mash them by hand.
Keep the sparkling water ice-cold and mix the batter just before frying for the crispest coating.
Raw garlic gets stronger as the dip sits, so make it a few hours ahead if you like it mellow, or use 3 cloves.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Skordalia keeps covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; let it sit at room temperature 30 minutes and loosen with a little water before serving. The fried cod is best eaten straight away. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
